key_insight: AtomFlow speeds up neutral-atom quantum control by putting imaging analysis and atom rearrangement directly on one FPGA, removing host-side round-trip delays.
engineering_relevance: This shows that tightly integrated FPGA pipelines can turn classical control overhead from a bottleneck into a scalable, low-latency hardware datapath for quantum systems.
method: Co-locates fluorescence-image analysis and atom rearrangement on a single Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA.
Streams rearrangement moves immediately as they are computed instead of waiting for batch completion.
Uses an end-to-end control architecture designed for neutral-atom quantum computer operation.
evidence_signal: On a 16x16 atom array, the system reports 25.3 ms end-to-end latency, 4 ms first-move latency, and about 1 ms average move generation time.
watch_item: The approach is promising, but practical deployment still depends on staying within FPGA resource limits as array size and control complexity grow.
paper_title: AtomFlow: An End-to-End FPGA-Based Control Architecture for Neutral Atom Quantum Computers
